title: Advanced Colorway Assigning | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive
description:

summary: # Advanced Colorway Assigning | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, it's Phoebe, and I have another great update for you regarding Colorway, especially on how you can assign it. So let's jump on in and have some fun while we learn. I wanted to create a separate video for this because I know assigning is a little bit more difficult now. I aim to provide a brief review of how we can add in colorways and all of that. ## Colorway Assignment Methods As a reminder, there are now two ways to manage colorways: 1. **Simple Method**: This is the method that I feel like 90% of you should still keep doing. 2. **Robust Method**: This allows you to add in custom settings for your colorways. ### Understanding Materials and Properties - **Materials**: This refers to the material part of the property editor. - **All Properties**: This encompasses all the properties in the property editor. - **Linking**: This means linking all properties, including materials, together. When we say "properties," think of the property editor. You can, of course, do this by each fabric. All of these are just material variations. All the colors can be different, and all of the textures can be different, but at the end of the day, the physical properties of all of these remain the same. ## Example Fabric I just created a random fabric here that’s bright red to help us understand these differences. You can also see the colorway changes. ### Drag and Drop Functionality As a refresher, you can drag and drop in both the 3D and the colorway window. If you drag and drop in the 3D window, please be aware that you are editing the pattern—not the whole colorway. If you're editing the pattern, you're modifying certain parts of your design. ### Options for Assignment - **Current Colorway Only**: Assigning to the current colorway means that only this one colorway will be affected; none of the other ones will be. - **Assign to All Colorways by Unlinking Materials**: This affects all colorways, but only the materials part of the property editor will be unlinked. - **Assign to All Colorways by Linking Everything Together**: This means all the colors will change, all of the properties will change—everything. For example, if I assign to the current colorway, only this one colorway is going to be affected. If I drag and drop, this will only affect the specific pattern piece and this one colorway. ## Managing Colorway Changes If I switch to a different colorway (e.g., Colorway A) and select the same exact pattern piece, you can see that this is still Fabric 1. If I go to Colorway 1 and select this pattern piece, you now see that this is Fabric 1, not Fabric 01. ### Undoing Changes If I need to undo my changes, I can hit `Ctrl + Z` multiple times. If I drag and drop while holding `Ctrl` and select "Assign to All Colorways by Unlinking Materials," this will affect all colorways, but the only property I can change is the material part of it. The fabric property will be overwritten, but I can change all of the materials across the colorways. ## Example of Colorway Updates When I drag and drop, every single colorway will now show this red pattern once I hit update. This is how all of them will work because I'm changing the pattern, not the fabric. ### Linking All Properties If I select "Link All Properties," I can drag and drop in the 3D window, and you will see a little link option. If I change any of these colors, they will all change together. For instance, if I change this to green, all of them become green. ## Colorway Editor Options You have the same three options when you drag and drop into your colorway editor: 1. **Current Colorway Only**: Changes only this specific colorway. 2. **All Colorways by Unlinking Materials**: Allows linking the colors but keeps materials separate. 3. **Link All Properties**: Links all properties, including material changes. ### Example of Colorway Editor Usage If I drag and drop on top of a colorway, this will only affect that specific colorway. All others remain unchanged. ## User Settings Update Now that I’ve covered how to assign colorways, let me go over the update. In your user settings, navigate to the top toolbar, then to settings, and finally to user settings. Under "Other," you will find the colorway options. You can choose whether you want to assign to the current colorway only or assign to all colorways as your default option. For example, if you typically choose to assign to all colorways, you can set this as your default. ## Conclusion I hope you find this recap helpful! If you have any questions, please use the comment section below, and someone will get back to you. Don’t forget to like and subscribe, and check out all of our Clo videos on our YouTube channel for more great information. Thanks again for watching, and keep having fun in Clo!
